alternatives_considered.approach: Bayesian conjugate posterior for the evaluator instead of a normal-approx z-test
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: L2 Bayesian machinery is heavier than the ticket needs; the z-test with a min-sample gate deterministically produces the required first-class inconclusive, and L3/L4 methods are explicitly out of scope

alternatives_considered.approach: Storing only the final score instead of all eight components
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: TR-18 requires stored score components so the ranker's own calibration can be evaluated later; a bare score is undebuggable

work_order.approach: Add two pure domain modules (no IO, {code,message,details} errors): src/domain/opportunities.js implements the spec section 26 formula Score = value x pSuccess x fit x infoValue x reversibility / cost / downside / delay with divisor floors (cost, downside, delay each floored at 1 so a zero cost can never divide by zero or score infinite); the ONLY rank key everywhere is stored score desc, id asc (expectedContribution is a stored display field, never a sort key). src/domain/experiments.js implements L1 native A/B evaluation as a min-sample gate plus a two-proportion z-test at |z| >= 1.96 returning win/loss/inconclusive, with 'inconclusive' a persisted experiment state (enum draft|running|matured|stopped|inconclusive). Persist behind tenant-bound tables (migration 005: opportunities and experiments rows are mutable working state with NO immutability trigger; only the new experiment_evaluations table is append-only with decisions-pattern triggers), expose POST/GET /v1/opportunities plus POST/GET /v1/experiments and POST /v1/experiments/:id/evaluate (which INSERTs an evaluation row and UPDATEs experiments.state to matured on win/loss or inconclusive otherwise) with the standard error envelope and idempotent re-posts, render the ranked list ordered by stored score with all eight components and experiment cards with caps/stop/state-badge/data-through from the repositories (replacing the dead opportunity.scored/experiment.started raw-event reads nothing ever writes), keep the composer draft in localStorage so fetch failures preserve it, and seed three ranked opportunities plus one running and one inconclusive experiment. Meta-first per the recorded answer: no Google experiment adapter; native A/B plus Bayesian levels only.

files.change: Pure module: validateOpportunity (opp_ id prefix, tenant_id, all eight components with types; cost/downside as numbers floored at 1 for divisors, delay days floored at 1, probabilities/fit/reversibility/info in documented ranges), scoreOpportunity (spec section 26 formula with divisor floors of 1), rankOpportunities (score desc, id asc — the ONLY rank key; no contribution-based ordering anywhere), expectedContribution (derived display field only, integer micros: trunc(value_micros * pSuccess) - cost_micros, never used for sorting). Pinned computed examples: generic value=1000 p=0.5 fit=0.8 info=1.2 rev=0.9 cost=100 downside=2 delay=1 yields 2.16; cheap fixture value=2000 p=0.2 fit=0.5 info=0.8 rev=0.5 cost=100 downside=2 delay=1 yields 0.40 with contribution 300M micros; expensive fixture value=6000 p=0.6 fit=0.9 info=1.2 rev=0.9 cost=1900 downside=2 delay=1 yields 0.9208 with contribution 1700M micros, so the expensive campaign wins on the pinned rank key AND on contribution. Invariant: every list surface orders by stored score desc then id asc; scores are finite positive numbers. Errors as {code,message,details} with codes OPP_BAD_ID, OPP_BAD_COMPONENT, OPP_BAD_MONEY. Never imports node:sqlite.

Pure module: validateExperiment (exp_ id prefix, tenant_id, arms [{id, name}], caps {max_spend_micros integer > 0, max_downside_micros integer > 0}, stopRules {min_runtime_hours, min_sample integer > 0, success_threshold, harm_threshold}, state one of draft|running|matured|stopped|inconclusive where inconclusive is the persisted first-class card state for underpowered or no-separation outcomes, data_through UTC ISO-8601), evaluateExperiment ({control_conversions, control_exposures, treatment_conversions, treatment_exposures, min_sample, threshold z=1.96}: total conversions < min_sample yields {outcome: inconclusive, reason: underpowered, next_state: inconclusive}; else two-proportion z-test, |z| < 1.96 yields {outcome: inconclusive, reason: no-separation, next_state: inconclusive}, sign yields {outcome: win|loss, next_state: matured}; never forced), stopRuleTriggered (harm threshold or cap breach). Computed example: 10/1000 vs 12/1000 with min_sample 100 yields inconclusive reason underpowered (22 total < 100). Codes EXP_BAD_ID, EXP_BAD_ARMS, EXP_BAD_CAPS, EXP_BAD_STOP_RULES. No IO imports.

Add migration 005_opportunity_experiment_tables creating three tables: opportunities (tenant_id, opportunity_id PK, record JSON holding all eight components, score REAL stored at write time, created_at) and experiments (tenant_id, experiment_id PK, record JSON, state TEXT, evaluation_result TEXT nullable, evaluation_reason TEXT nullable, evaluated_at TEXT nullable, data_through TEXT, created_at) are BOTH mutable working state with deliberately NO immutability trigger, so UPDATEs to score/state/data_through/evaluation columns always succeed; experiment_evaluations (tenant_id, experiment_id, evaluated_at, result, reason, counts JSON, PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, experiment_id, evaluated_at)) is append-only with BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers matching the decisions pattern (RAISE ABORT). Tenant-ordered indexes on opportunities (tenant_id, score DESC, opportunity_id) and experiments (tenant_id, created_at, experiment_id).

Add opportunities, experiments and evaluations repositories: opportunities.create (idempotent INSERT OR IGNORE on the fixed id storing record JSON plus computed score, returns {created, row}), opportunities.get, opportunities.list (ORDER BY score DESC, opportunity_id ASC — the single rank key — binding tenant_id, parsing record JSON back to the domain object); experiments.create/get/list (ORDER BY created_at, experiment_id) plus experiments.updateState (UPDATEs state, evaluation_result, evaluation_reason, evaluated_at, data_through for the tenant-bound row — legal because no trigger guards this table); evaluations.append (INSERT into experiment_evaluations) and evaluations.listForExperiment. No update/delete surface for evaluations.

Add POST /v1/opportunities (validateOpportunity, 400 on invalid with stable code; stores record including computed score and all eight components; idempotent re-post returns existing with created:false), GET /v1/opportunities (ranked list straight from repositories.opportunities.list, already score-desc/id-asc, with components and score per row), POST /v1/experiments (validateExperiment, same idempotency), GET /v1/experiments (cards payload: id, name, state, evaluation_result, evaluation_reason, caps, stopRules, data_through), POST /v1/experiments/:id/evaluate (422 UNKNOWN_EXPERIMENT when missing; runs evaluateExperiment over the posted counts, INSERTs the evaluation row, then UPDATEs experiments.state to the returned next_state — matured on win/loss, inconclusive on inconclusive — plus evaluated_at/data_through). All failures use the {code,message} envelope, never stacks.

Rewrite opportunities() and experiments() sections to read repositories.opportunities.list / repositories.experiments.list instead of the placeholder opportunity.scored/experiment.started raw events. Ranked rows render name, stored score and all eight components with data-testid opportunity-row/score-components, in repository order (never re-sorted in the view). Experiment cards render name, caps (max spend formatted via formatMoney, max downside), stop rules text, state badge (data-testid exp-state; state inconclusive renders the badge text Inconclusive with the evaluation reason beside it) and data-through timestamp with data-testid experiment-card/caps/stop-rules/data-through. Add the hypothesis composer form (title, thesis, suggested cap inputs with labels) on /experiments. Keep the five states and existing empty/error copy; partial banner keeps provisional-scores wording.

Persist the hypothesis composer fields to localStorage on input and restore them on load, so the error shell (which keeps the form mounted beside the error panel) never loses a draft; keep the existing retry/drawer behaviour unchanged. Keys namespaced opp_exp_draft_.

Seed three opportunities with fixed opp_ ids whose stored scores order deterministically: opp_seed_expensive (expensive high-quality fixture: value=6000 p=0.6 fit=0.9 info=1.2 rev=0.9 cost=1900 downside=2 delay=1, score 0.9208, contribution 1700M micros), opp_seed_cheap (cheap low-quality fixture: value=2000 p=0.2 fit=0.5 info=0.8 rev=0.5 cost=100 downside=2 delay=1, score 0.40, contribution 300M micros), opp_seed_low (value=1000 p=0.2 fit=0.4 info=0.5 rev=0.5 cost=500 downside=2 delay=2, score 0.01); and two experiments with fixed exp_ ids: exp_seed_running (state running with caps, stop rules, data-through timestamp) and exp_seed_underpowered (state inconclusive, evaluation_result inconclusive, evaluation_reason underpowered, with caps, stop rules, data-through timestamp). work_order.understanding: Issue #22 is the strategist slice of epic #14: rank competing bets with stored score components (spec section 26 opportunity economy: value x pSuccess x fit x infoValue x reversibility / cost / downside / delay) and settle them with L1/L2 experiments (native A/B plus Bayesian levels) that carry caps, stop rules and a first-class inconclusive state, reusing the quality funnel (qualified CPL over downstream events) so a cheap low-quality campaign loses to an expensive high-quality one. The codebase today has no scoring or evaluation code: src/web/pages.js renders opportunities/experiments from placeholder raw events (opportunity.scored, experiment.started) that nothing ever writes, and there is no src/domain/opportunities.js, src/domain/experiments.js, no tables, and no API for either. Dependencies #19 (decision journal) and #21 (research mesh plus learnings) are merged, so the decision record, research-observations panel and retrieval gate exist to consume. The recorded human answer (Meta Ads first, Google after) means no Google experiment adapter in this slice.

triage.diagnosis: The qa agent did not fail — it succeeded (45 turns, ~6 min, 25 evidence files, 24 cited and all present). The failure is in the separate judge job: `sdlc-ctl.mjs validate --schema qa-report` rejected the report because tests[10] (the 11th of 12 test entries) omits the required `status` field. `status` is a required per-test property with enum pass|fail|blocked|skipped and no default, so — unlike the 12 cosmetic `steps` scalar-to-array slips the validator auto-repaired on the same pass — a missing verdict is a semantic fact the validator cannot invent; the tester alone knows whether that test passed. The report, not the testing, is the broken artifact, so there is nothing to resume: the browser evidence lives only in this run's `qa-evidence` artifact and is not rehydrated into the next runner's QA_EVIDENCE_DIR, and the pipeline explicitly tells the rerun to re-test rather than copy its results. The work order (AC-1..AC-6) and the app under test are sound — no test failed and no app bug surfaced, so nothing to repair or replan. This is a non-deterministic model-output slip on a first occurrence (the only prior signature on this issue, ci:unknown:8585c515b6416cdc, is a different type), and the next qa run is not a blind repeat: previous-output.json now carries the rejected report and this exact reason, so the agent is told precisely what to correct. Not a network flake or outage — 'transient' here means a one-off agent-formatting error that the corrective-feedback rerun is designed to clear.
